texts.li: [fire,lowtech] A fire started in a bakehouse at {PLACE} and went through the thatch faster than the bucket lines could follow. A quarter of the town is ash, and {FACTION} are sleeping under carts and in the temple.\n\n{DEAD}, who speaks for the town now, has sent a rider to the colony with a list: what they need to rebuild before the weather turns, and what they'll pay for it.

[fire,!lowtech] A fire broke out in a fuel store at {PLACE} and took a whole street with it before {FACTION} got it under control. Families are sleeping in the school hall.\n\n{DEAD}, who's running the rebuilding, has sent a courier to the colony with a list of what they need, and a price for all of it.

[storm,lowtech] A storm came down the valley two nights ago and took the roofs off half of {PLACE}. {FACTION} have saved what they could, and the rest is in the river.\n\n{DEAD} has sent a rider to the colony to ask whether it can sell them what they need to put the roofs back, by a set day.

[storm,!lowtech] A windstorm tore through {PLACE} two nights ago: roofs gone, walls down, the power lines in the street. {FACTION} are patching what they can.\n\n{DEAD}, who's in charge of the rebuilding, has sent a list to the colony and asked for help, for a fair price.

[flood] The river came up over its banks at {PLACE} and stood in the streets for three days. The lower town is mud to the windowsills, and {FACTION} are digging out.\n\n{DEAD} has sent word to the colony: they need building materials and food for the work crews, by a set day, and they'll pay well for them.

terms.li: What {FACTION} need: {ITEM}. Everything has to be in the colony's stockpiles within {DAYS} of the colony agreeing.\n\nFor all of it, they'll pay {COUNT} silver, well over its worth. If at least half of everything is ready, they'll take that and pay its plain worth. With less, they'll go elsewhere, and remember it.

accepted.li: [fire] The colony has agreed to help {PLACE} rebuild after the fire: {ITEM}, within {DAYS}. {FACTION}'s carts will come for it.
[storm] The colony has agreed to help {PLACE} put its roofs back: {ITEM}, within {DAYS}. {FACTION}'s carts will come for it.
[flood] The colony has agreed to help {PLACE} dig out after the flood: {ITEM}, within {DAYS}. {FACTION}'s carts will come for it.

ready.li: Everything {PLACE} needs to rebuild is ready. {FACTION}'s carts will come for it in {DAYS}.

reminder.li: {FACTION}'s carts come for the building materials within {DAYS}: {ITEM}.

done.li: [delivered,fire] {FACTION}'s carts came at first light and loaded everything the colony had set aside, and {DEAD} counted out {ITEM} silver on the tailboard. The new houses at {PLACE} will have the colony's timber in their walls.\n\n{FACTION} won't forget who helped them back on their feet.

[delivered,storm] {FACTION}'s carts came for the materials and went home loaded to the rails. {DEAD} paid {ITEM} silver, and says the roofs at {PLACE} will be back on before the next storm.\n\n{FACTION} won't forget it.

[delivered,flood] {FACTION}'s carts came for everything the colony set aside, and {DEAD} paid {ITEM} silver. The work crews at {PLACE} are eating the colony's food while they shovel out the colony's neighbors.\n\n{FACTION} won't forget it.
[partial] {FACTION}'s carts came and found only part of what they'd asked for ready. They loaded what there was, paid its plain worth, {ITEM} silver, and went to find the rest somewhere else.

fail.li: [missed] {FACTION}'s carts came for the materials and found far too little ready. They left empty, and {PLACE} will be rebuilding slower than it hoped.\n\n{FACTION} think less of the colony for the broken promise.

[missed,fire] {FACTION}'s carts came for the timber and left with almost nothing. The burned street at {PLACE} will stand empty a while longer, and {DEAD} has said so, in a letter the colony would rather not have received.

cancelled.li: {FACTION} are no longer on terms with the colony, and the order for {PLACE} is off.

texts.li: [winter,lowtech] The harvest at {PLACE} came in thin, and {FACTION} won't have enough laid by to see the winter out. {DEAD}, who keeps the town's stores, has sent a rider to the colony with a list: food that keeps, firewood, and cloth or hides for winter coats, by a set day.

[winter,!lowtech] {FACTION}'s granary at {PLACE} took water in the autumn rains, and half of it spoiled. {DEAD}, their quartermaster, has sent a courier with a list of what they'll need to get through the winter, and a good price for all of it.

[drought] The rains failed at {PLACE} this year. The wells are low, the fields are dust, and {FACTION} are eating their seed grain. {DEAD} has sent a rider to the colony: they need food, and medicine for the fevers that come with bad water, and they'll pay what they can.

[sickness,lowtech] A sickness is going round {PLACE}, the kind that keeps people in bed for a week and leaves them weak. {DEAD}, their healer, has turned the meeting hall into a sickhouse, and has sent to the colony for medicine, food and clean cloth.

[sickness,!lowtech] {FACTION}'s clinic at {PLACE} is full: a bad flu, nothing worse, but enough to empty the shelves. {DEAD}, who runs the clinic, has sent a courier with an order: medicine, meals for the patients and cloth for bandages and bedding, by a set day.

terms.li: What {FACTION} need: {ITEM}. Everything has to be in the colony's stockpiles, and the food still fresh, within {DAYS} of the colony agreeing.\n\nFor all of it, they'll pay {COUNT} silver, well over its worth. If at least half of everything is ready, they'll take that and pay its plain worth. With less, they'll go elsewhere, and remember it.

accepted.li: [winter] The colony has agreed to help {PLACE} through the winter: {ITEM}, within {DAYS}. {FACTION}'s carts will come for it.
[drought] The colony has agreed to send {PLACE} food and medicine for the dry year: {ITEM}, within {DAYS}. {FACTION}'s carts will come for it.
[sickness] The colony has agreed to supply {DEAD}'s sickhouse at {PLACE}: {ITEM}, within {DAYS}. {FACTION}'s carts will come for it.

ready.li: Everything {PLACE} asked for is ready. {FACTION}'s carts will come for it in {DAYS}.

reminder.li: {FACTION}'s carts come for the provisions within {DAYS}: {ITEM}.

done.li: [delivered,winter] {FACTION}'s carts came for the winter stores and went home loaded, and {DEAD} paid {ITEM} silver without haggling. {PLACE} will see the winter out.\n\n{FACTION} won't forget who filled their storehouse.

[delivered,drought] {FACTION}'s carts came for the food and medicine and went home heavy. {DEAD} paid {ITEM} silver, and says the colony has kept {PLACE} alive until the rains come back.\n\n{FACTION} won't forget it.

[delivered,sickness] {FACTION}'s carts came for the supplies, and {DEAD} paid {ITEM} silver and sent word a week later: the sickhouse at {PLACE} is emptying, and everyone who went in has walked out.\n\n{FACTION} won't forget it.
[partial] {FACTION}'s carts came and found only part of what they'd asked for ready. They loaded what there was, paid its plain worth, {ITEM} silver, and went to find the rest somewhere else.

fail.li: [missed] {FACTION}'s carts came and found far too little ready. They went home empty, and {PLACE} will have to find what it needs elsewhere, if it can.\n\n{FACTION} think less of the colony for the broken promise.
[missed,sickness] {FACTION}'s carts came for the sickhouse supplies and left nearly empty. {DEAD} wrote afterwards: they managed, barely, and won't be asking the colony again.

cancelled.li: {FACTION} are no longer on terms with the colony, and the order for {PLACE} is off.
